channel.title: # 🇱🇰 This Week in Sri Lanka
channel.description: Generated by gpt-5 from 284 English News Articles published between 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-17.

item.title: Death toll from prison riots climbed to 31 as watchdogs opened inquiries.
item.description: A national human-rights body (an independent commission empowered by statute to investigate abuses) launched a multi-pronged probe into the violence, access denial at a major remand facility, and claims of ill‑treatment during subsequent transfers. Forensic teams said 14 deaths were caused by gunshot wounds, while nine resulted from severe head trauma inflicted with blunt objects. Hundreds of detainees were moved to other jails, and the officer who fired live rounds during the breach was reassigned pending internal checks. Separately, officials disclosed that the prison population has surged to more than 42,000, intensifying scrutiny of overcrowding, security lapses, and allegations of torture.

item.title: Legal fraternity united against plan to extend top judges’ tenure.
item.description: Bar leaders warned that changing the retirement age of superior‑court judges risks eroding confidence in the bench and upsetting career progression in the lower judiciary. Magistrates and district judges voted unanimously to oppose the move, while the cabinet spokesman said no final decision had been reached and more information had been sought. Lawyers also pressed to fill long‑standing vacancies on the apex courts, citing four empty seats in each tier and the President’s constitutional duty under Article 107(1) (the clause assigning appointments to the Head of State) to act without delay. Multiple regional bar associations echoed those concerns and questioned the timing of any tenure change.

item.title: Government launched Rs. 51bn scheme to bring safe water to 67,000 households in the North Central dry zone.
item.description: The utility said the project will build a treatment plant and lay more than 1,500 kilometres of distribution lines to serve areas long affected by chronic kidney disease. Funding comes from a Japanese aid agency (JICA, the Japan International Cooperation Agency) alongside the Treasury, with work slated to finish within three years. Officials described the scheme as the country’s second‑largest water investment and said it complements future canal links to bolster resilience in drought‑prone districts. The programme’s public‑health goal is to cut exposure to unsafe groundwater.

item.title: Dengue cases topped 71,000 with Western Province hardest hit.
item.description: Health trackers reported 1,284 new infections in a single day, taking fatalities to 49 this year and pushing cumulative incidence well beyond seasonal norms. The national control unit (a surveillance body coordinating vector control and clinical guidance) urged early medical care for warning signs and intensified source‑reduction in urban hotspots. Colombo and Gampaha districts accounted for the largest shares of notified illnesses, while authorities warned that heavy rains and standing water continue to fuel transmission. Public messaging focused on household container cleanup and rapid triage for severe symptoms.

item.title: Police warned motorists of phishing texts masquerading as unpaid speeding fines.
item.description: Investigators said messages mimic official payment portals and redirect users to fake sites to harvest credentials, advising the public to check for .gov.lk domains and delete suspicious links. Phishing (a fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive data by impersonating a trusted entity) has also involved app downloads that install remote‑access malware.

item.title: Environment ministry launched a US$38.2m programme to curb mercury and hazardous waste in labs and hospitals.
item.description: The five‑year effort is backed by the Global Environment Facility and UNDP and includes phasing out mercury‑containing medical devices in line with the Minamata Convention (a global treaty to protect human health from mercury). Officials also handed over advanced analytical equipment to strengthen chemical monitoring.

item.title: Cabinet spokesman said inmate numbers swelled to over 42,000 since 2024 anti‑drug drive.
item.description: The briefing linked the surge to the ‘Ratama Ekata’ operations and outlined new recruitment and building projects, including a high‑security unit at a naval base to house higher‑risk detainees. Recently completed prison blocks and storage upgrades were cited as short‑term steps to ease congestion.

item.title: Tourism receipts hit US$1.51bn in the first half as June revenue fell less than arrivals.
item.description: June earnings of US$151.1 million were down 10.9% year‑on‑year even as the new statistical method tracking visitor nights softened the drop versus raw headcounts. The benchmark for average daily spend was revised to US$148, and meeting the year‑end goal now requires roughly US$2.0 billion in the second half.

item.title: State oil buyer added two Russian suppliers to its eligible roster.
item.description: The managing director said Rosneft Oil and Zarubezhneft have been registered to bid at the next crude tender opening on 21 July, expanding competition for refinery feedstock. Around 15 companies are now on the books for supply opportunities.

item.title: Cabinet cleared a $35m loan and grants for grid‑linked rooftop solar and virtual net metering.
item.description: The package comprises an Asian Development Bank facility plus €15.4 million from the EU and $5.5 million from Japan to integrate small producers into the power system. Virtual net metering (a crediting mechanism that offsets customer bills using energy from remote or aggregated panels) will help scale participation by households and SMEs.
